text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:

- Opposition parties are threatening to end cooperation with the minority government unless their views are considered in land reform matters. Their objections mainly concern the privatisation of land.

- The defence ministry is to sue the magazine LUUP for slander. The magazine said last week that the ministry concluded a deal with a fuel firm, which costs the state several million kroons extra every year.

- The president rejected the appeals of three murderers condemned to death, but the sentence was replaced by life imprisonment since the authorities had deliberately delayed their execution for three years.
- Economy Minister Jaak Leemann announced that the monopoly in metal exports granted to the EMEX state-owned company, will be abolished as against a law on fair business.
- The director of Tallinn central prison left his post yesterday and the prosecuting office has started an investigation of his activities.
- A mistake by an energy network official led to a brief power blackout in Tallinn and a 20-minute one in the Harju county yesterday.
- MP Ando Leps demanded explanations yesterday about the disappearance of a large number of KGB dossiers before their taking by the security police.
- Health care service trade union demands wages rise for doctors and nurses: their average salary was 2,819 kroons this year's first quarter, while the national average is 3,136 kroons.
- The government will not repress illegal residents, Prime Minister Mart Siimann assured in a radio broadcast yesterday.
- The Moderate faction appealed to the chancellor of justice to find out whether the Tallinn city council members Edgar Savisaar and Peeter Sepp legally belonging to the council.
- A Finnish firm plans to build a 50 million kroon chemical product terminal in Paldiski port with annual capacity of 300,000 tons.
- Singaporean investor Tolaram Group wants to buy the former army barracks in Tondi, Tallinn to establish a science and technology park there.
